newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-WENGER PROMISES INQUEST AFTER ARSENAL SEE RED AGAIN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-WENGER PROMISES INQUEST AFTER ARSENAL SEE RED AGAIN.

text.p: Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger promised an inquest after forward John Hartson became the side's fourth player to be sent off in eight games during Wednesday's 2-0 defeat of Middlesbrough.
"I must speak with John Hartson because it is always stupid to speak to the referee," Wenger said. "We are having too many red and yellow cards.
"Sometimes you can understand them because they are for tackles in the game, but this one was outside the game and less understandable."
Hartson, who came on as a 65th minute substitute for Dutch striker Dennis Bergkamp, was booked for a 89th minute foul on Middlesbrough player-manager Bryan Robson.
Referee Mike Reed then showed him the red card less than 30 seconds later for "foul and abusive language".

The Welsh international will now be suspended for three games for the second time this season. The ban is due to begin in a fortnight's time, just as Arsenal's key striker Ian Wright returns from a similar suspension, imposed after he was sent off at Nottingham Forest last month.
"My big worries now are losing too many players with suspensions and injuries," Wenger said. "I cannot condemn the behaviour of my team, but they are getting too many cards.
"Of course now we will miss Ian Wright, but we will just have to find other ways to score."
Hartson and Wright followed in the footsteps of centre-backs Tony Adams and Steve Bould, sent off against Newcastle and Liverpool respectively earlier this season.
And combined with injuries to goalkeeper David Seaman, David Platt, Lee Dixon and Remi Garde, the suspensions are threatening to scupper Arsenal's hopes of lifting their 11th English league title.

On the brighter side for Arsenal, Wright's strike in Wednesday's victory was his 200th league goal. He scored 89 times in the league for Crystal Palace before crossing the Thames to join the north Londoners.
It also takes his tally this season to 23 in all competitions and brings him to within 12 goals of the club's all-time scoring record of 178 goals, set by Cliff Bastin in the 1930s.
